description:
Episode 121 of a daily journey through the universe. ⭐
We visit Orion's Belt: Alnitak, Alnilam and Mintaka, three hot blue giant stars that only look lined up, roughly 700 to 2,000 light-years away, plus the Horsehead and Flame nebulas and the Orion Nebula just below, the sword where stars are being born.

segments.text: Episode one hundred and twenty-one. Next stop... Orion's Belt.
Three bright stars in a row. Probably the most famous pattern in the night sky.
segments.headline: Three stars in a row

segments.text: Their names are Alnitak, Alnilam and Mintaka.
segments.headline: Alnitak, Alnilam, Mintaka

segments.text: They look like neighbors, but they're not. They sit hundreds to about two thousand light-years away. They only line up from our point of view.
All three are hot blue giant stars, each shining many thousands of times brighter than the Sun.
Next to Alnitak hide two famous clouds: the Flame Nebula, and the dark Horsehead Nebula.
segments.headline: The Horsehead Nebula

segments.text: Below the Belt hangs Orion's sword. Its middle star isn't a star at all.
segments.headline: Orion's sword

segments.text: It's the Orion Nebula, a star nursery about one thousand three hundred light-years away, where new stars are being born right now.
segments.headline: A star nursery

segments.text: Many cultures saw something different in these stars: a hunter, three kings, a fishing line, or three sisters.
segments.headline: Many stories

segments.text: Tomorrow, a ghostly glow that rises after sunset in spring. Most people have never seen it. Follow, so you don't miss episode one hundred and twenty-two.
